subject: Client request: DPA amendment & subprocessor clarity — action plan for product/security sign-off
messages:
From: Tom Keller <procurement@smartapps.io>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <legal@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: DPA amendment — analytics telemetry carveout

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the demo last week — excited about where this could go. Our legal team has a few required edits to Redwood's standard DPA before procurement can move forward. High-level asks:

- A narrow data-use carveout allowing Acme Analytics to retain aggregated telemetry for billing and feature analytics (we're proposing a 90-day retention window).
- Clarification and explicit listing of subprocessors used for telemetry/analytics processing (we need vendor names + regions).
- A clause limiting any commercial use of Acme data; specifically, Redwood must not use raw customer data to improve open models.

I've attached our annotated redline (Acme_DPA_client_redline_v1.pdf). Can you loop in product and security — we need their signoff on operational feasibility and risk mitigation before legal will accept the language.

Can we target next-week (Nov 27) to have a reconciled position? If helpful, happy to do a 30m call.

Thanks,
Tom
Procurement, SmartApps (on behalf of Acme Analytics)

Attachments: Acme_DPA_client_redline_v1.pdf (PDF, 128KB)
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Keller <procurement@smartapps.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: DPA amendment — analytics telemetry carveout

Tom — thanks for the clear redline and timeline. Looping in Legal (Laura), Product (Dev), and Security (Hannah) so we can take a cross-functional look.

Proposed next steps / MAP:
1) Product to confirm technical implications of the 90-day telemetry carveout and whether telemetry can be aggregated/anonymized without impacting product telemetry pipelines (Dev). Target: 2026-11-23.
2) Security to confirm what attestations we can provide (SOC2, encryption at rest, access controls) and whether an exception is required for any subprocessor. Target: 2026-11-24.
3) Legal to provide reconciled redlines and non-negotiables for procurement. Target: 2026-11-26.
4) Consolidated response to Acme by 2026-11-27 and optional 30m call on 2026-11-28 if needed.

Laura/Dev/Hannah — please reply with quick notes against the redline (I've attached the file forwarded from Acme).

— Rafael
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Acme_DPA_client_redline_v1.pdf (forwarded)
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Keller <procurement@smartapps.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: DPA amendment — analytics telemetry carveout

Thanks Rafael / Tom — quick technical read:

- 90-day retention for aggregated telemetry is generally feasible if the data remains aggregated and not tied to PII or interaction-level traces. Our telemetry pipeline currently retains raw request metadata (timestamps, route, token counts) for 180 days for debugging and model quality. Shortening to 90 days will require changes to retention policy and could increase troubleshooting time for incidents.

- If Acme is comfortable with a strictly aggregated view (e.g., daily summaries by route, no request-level logs), we can implement a 90-day aggregated retention and keep raw logs for 30 days for emergency debugging (we'd treat those raw logs as restricted and only used under incident response).

- Subprocessors: our telemetry currently flows through two vendors for analytics and log storage — LogStorm (EU & US) and CloudArchive (US). If Acme requires removal of either vendor or a particular region, that will materially impact our cost and ingestion architecture; we can discuss mitigation (e.g., routing Acme traffic to US-only storage) but that may increase latency/cost.

Questions for Acme (Tom/Maya):
1) Is request-level log access ever required for your compliance?
2) Are you willing to accept aggregated-only telemetry for analytics?

I'll draft concise technical language for the DPA carveout and flag the parts where security needs to add controls.

— Dev
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Keller <procurement@smartapps.io>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: DPA amendment — analytics telemetry carveout

Tom / Rafael — attached are legal's comments and a proposed reconciled redline (Compiled_Redlines_20261127.docx). High-level positions:

- We can accept a limited telemetry carveout so long as it is clearly defined (aggregated metrics only; no model training on customer raw content; explicit retention period). Suggested wording: "Provider may retain aggregated telemetry for billing and product analytics purposes for up to 90 days; Provider shall not use customer content for model training or for creating derivative datasets for commercial purposes."

- Subprocessors: Acme's ask for an explicit vendor list is reasonable. We can provide an initial subprocessor registry (LogStorm, CloudArchive) and commit to 30 days notice before adding new subprocessors. Procurement may request longer notice — propose 60 days if acceptable.

- We cannot accept an open-ended prohibition on any vendor usage; instead propose contractual mitigations (DPA schedule listing current subprocessors, region scoping, and the notice period).

I'll mark non-negotiable clauses in the attached doc. If Acme insists on removing LogStorm, we'll need their security/technical team to accept routing to US-only storage and the associated latency cost delta.

— Laura
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Compiled_Redlines_20261127.docx (Word, 52KB)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Keller <procurement@smartapps.io>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: DPA amendment — analytics telemetry carveout

Tom / team — security perspective: 

- We can provide SOC 2 Type II and a supplemental security attestation for Acme. We will redact internal-only traces but can provide summary audit logs quarterly.

- Regarding subprocessors: LogStorm (EU/US) is used for analytics indexing; CloudArchive is retained backup storage (US). If Acme wants to exclude LogStorm entirely, we need to: 1) route their ingestion to US-only pipeline, and 2) sign a commercial addendum for the increased storage/egress cost.

- Retention suggestion: Product's proposed approach (90-day aggregated + 30-day restricted raw logs for incident response) is acceptable provided:
  * Raw logs are accessed only under documented incident procedures,
  * Access is logged and auditable,
  * We include a clause to notify Acme within 72 hours of any access to raw logs.

- Additional ask: include a simple subprocessor security questionnaire (we can provide LogStorm's SOC2 summary and CloudArchive's security pack) as an appendix or link. That should satisfy procurement and speed signoff.

Happy to join a 30m call to walk through technical safeguards.

— Hannah
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Keller <procurement@smartapps.io>, Maya Singh <legal@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: DPA amendment — analytics telemetry carveout

Tom / Maya — thanks for the patience and detailed redline. Attached is our consolidated position and proposed language (Compiled_Redlines_20261127.docx). Quick summary for Acme: 

1) Telemetry: Redwood will provide aggregated-only telemetry for billing and product analytics with a 90-day retention window. We will retain raw request-level logs for up to 30 days strictly for incident response; access to raw logs will be auditable and Acme will be notified within 72 hours of any access.

2) Subprocessors: Current subprocessors for telemetry are LogStorm (EU & US) and CloudArchive (US). We will provide security packs (SOC2 summaries) for these vendors. Redwood will provide 60 days' notice before adding new subprocessors; immediate removal of a current subprocessor will require a migration plan and possible commercial adjustments.

3) Model training/commercial use: Redwood will not use Acme's raw customer content to train or improve models for commercial offerings. Aggregated, de-identified metrics are permitted for product analytics.

Next steps: 
- Legal (Laura) will circulate the final DPA language for signoff by EOD 2026-11-30.
- Security (Hannah) will upload the subprocessor security packs and an incident access SLAs link to the shared Drive.
- Product (Dev) will confirm implementation timeline (ETA for retention config changes and routing if Acme requests US-only).

If this looks acceptable, please confirm and we'll follow up with DocuSign. If you prefer, I'm available for a 30-minute alignment call on Mon Nov 29 at 10:00 PT.

Best,
Rafael
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
